fields.title: Nothing checks that a pull request names the agent that produced it

sections.What it checks:
* [std-PR.AGENT](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/134c546202285a1837fb2844058244b9ad9a91b1/examples/engineering/standards/common/pull-requests.md#agent-agent-produced-work-says-what-produced-it) says a pull request containing agent-produced work "**MUST** name
  the agent, the model and the prompt or task that produced it".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a pipeline job on each pull request. It reads the description and the commit messages. Where a commit has a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming an agent, or the description has a `## Produced by` heading, the job fails unless that section has an `Agent:`, a `Model:` and a `Task:` line.

The description is written after the code, so neither a pre-commit check nor a Claude Code hook on `Write` can see it.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the description is the only thing that notices a missing model or task today.

The check finds agent-produced work only where a trailer or a heading declares it. Whether a change is agent-produced at all is a reviewer's judgement. The standard fixes no layout for the three facts, so the check needs one agreed first. The rules about approval and self-merge belong to branch policy, and this check reads none of them.
